title: Section 5.0 Creating Field Aliases and Calculated Fields

source.author: Written for this study guide
source.grounding: help.splunk.com Splunk Enterprise 10.4, Knowledge Management Manual and props.conf spec

questions.stem: `clientip` is aliased to `src_ip`. What does `clientip=*` return afterwards?

options.text: The same events as before; both names now work.
options.explanation: An alias is added alongside the original field. It does not replace or remove anything, so both names are searchable.

options.text: Nothing, because the field is now called src_ip.
options.explanation: This assumes aliasing renames. It does not. Renaming is what the rename command does.

options.text: Only events indexed before the alias was created.
options.explanation: Aliases apply at search time to all matching events regardless of when they were indexed.

options.text: An error, because the field has been superseded.
options.explanation: No error occurs. Nothing about the original field changed.

questions.overallExplanation: An alias adds a second name for a field. The command that actually replaces a name is rename, and it only affects the result set of the one search it appears in.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use field aliases
guide.verdictNote: An alias is a knowledge object evaluated at step 5 of the nine search-time operations. rename is a search command operating downstream of all nine.

docs.title: Create field aliases in Splunk Web (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: A field alias does not replace or remove the original field name.

questions.stem: Two source fields, `userID` and `loginID`, should both be reachable as `user`. What does the documentation say about `FIELDALIAS-x = userID AS user loginID AS user`?

options.text: It is invalid; a single alias can only apply to one field, so only one of the two takes effect.
options.explanation: A field can have multiple aliases, but an alias name cannot be the destination for two different source fields in this way.

options.text: It is valid and merges both source fields into user.
options.explanation: This is the intuitive expectation and it is the documented failure case.

options.text: It is valid but the second alias overwrites the first on every event.
options.explanation: The configuration is not supported, so describing a deterministic overwrite rule misstates it.

options.text: It is valid only when both source fields are present on the same event.
options.explanation: Co-presence is not the issue. The configuration itself is documented as invalid.

questions.overallExplanation: Aliases are one-to-many, not many-to-one: one field can carry several alias names, but one alias name cannot collect several fields. The documented way to merge two fields into one is a calculated field using coalesce().

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use field aliases
guide.verdictNote: The working alternative is `EVAL-user = coalesce(userID, loginID)`, which is a calculated field and therefore runs at step 6, after aliasing at step 5.

docs.title: Configure field aliases with props.conf (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: A single field alias can only apply to one field.

questions.stem: Can a calculated field's eval expression reference a field added by an automatic lookup?

options.text: No. Calculated fields are evaluated before lookups in the search-time sequence.
options.explanation: Calculated fields run at step 6 and lookups at step 7, so the lookup output does not exist yet when the calculated field is evaluated.

options.text: Yes, as long as the lookup is defined in the same app.
options.explanation: App scope has no bearing on ordering. The sequence is fixed regardless of where the objects live.

options.text: Yes, because all search-time knowledge objects are evaluated together.
options.explanation: They are evaluated in a defined order, not simultaneously. That order is the whole point of this objective.

options.text: Only if the lookup is configured as a non-automatic lookup.
options.explanation: A manual lookup runs even later, as a search command, so it is further out of reach rather than closer.

questions.overallExplanation: Calculated fields can reference field extractions of every kind, but not lookups, event types or tags, because all three come later in the sequence. The order is worth memorising as the backbone of sections 4, 5, 6 and 9.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use calculated fields
guide.verdictNote: The nine search-time operations in order: field filters, EXTRACT-, REPORT-, KV_MODE, FIELDALIAS-, EVAL-, LOOKUP-, event types, tags.

docs.title: The sequence of search-time operations (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Calculated fields precede lookups, event types and tags.

questions.stem: A calculated field `EVAL-duration_ms` exists. Can it be given the CIM name `duration` by aliasing it?

options.text: No. Aliasing happens before calculated fields are evaluated, and the spec states you cannot alias a calculated field.
options.explanation: Aliasing is step 5 and calculated fields are step 6, so at aliasing time duration_ms does not yet exist.

options.text: Yes, provided the alias is defined in the same props.conf stanza.
options.explanation: Same-stanza placement does not change the order in which the two operations run.

options.text: Yes, because aliases are resolved last, after all field creation.
options.explanation: Aliases are resolved at step 5, not last. Tags are the final step.

options.text: Only if the calculated field is marked as a permanent field.
options.explanation: There is no such marking. Calculated fields exist only at search time.

questions.overallExplanation: Give the calculated field the name you want in the first place, or add a second calculated field. The general rule is directional: a calculated field can consume aliases, but an alias cannot consume a calculated field.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use calculated fields
guide.verdictNote: A related restriction: creating a calculated field on an aliased source is not supported, and a calculated field cannot be scoped to an aliased host, source or source type.

docs.title: props.conf spec (Admin Manual 10.4)
docs.note: You cannot alias a calculated field.

questions.stem: A props.conf stanza contains `EVAL-response_time = response_time/1000` and `EVAL-bitrate = bytes*1000/response_time`. What value of `response_time` does the bitrate calculation use?

options.text: The original extracted value, because all EVAL- settings in a stanza are processed in parallel.
options.explanation: The documentation states EVAL- configurations within a single props.conf stanza are processed in parallel rather than sequentially, so one cannot consume another's output.

options.text: The converted value, because the settings run in the order written.
options.explanation: Order in the file does not create a dependency chain. Parallel evaluation is explicit in the spec.

options.text: The converted value, because Splunk resolves dependencies automatically.
options.explanation: No dependency resolution takes place between calculated fields in the same stanza.

options.text: Neither; the configuration errors because response_time is defined twice.
options.explanation: Overriding an extracted field with a calculated field of the same name is allowed and does not error.

questions.overallExplanation: Calculated fields cannot chain within one stanza. Each EVAL- sees the field values as they were before any calculated field ran, so a calculation that depends on another has to be written out in full.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use calculated fields
guide.verdictNote: The exact wording is worth remembering: all EVAL-<fieldname> configurations within a single props.conf stanza are processed in parallel instead of sequentially.

docs.title: Configure calculated fields with props.conf (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: EVAL- settings in one stanza are processed in parallel, not sequentially.

questions.stem: In the Splunk Web form for a calculated field, what goes into the Eval Expression box?

options.text: The right-hand side only, for example `round(bytes/1024, 2)`
options.explanation: The field name is a separate form field, so the expression box holds the expression alone: no eval keyword and no assignment.

options.text: A full command, for example `eval kb = round(bytes/1024, 2)`
options.explanation: The leading eval keyword belongs to the search command, not to the configuration form.

options.text: An assignment without the keyword, for example `kb = round(bytes/1024, 2)`
options.explanation: The name is supplied separately, so repeating it in the expression is wrong.

options.text: A regular expression that matches the value to calculate
options.explanation: Regular expressions belong to field extractions. A calculated field takes an eval expression.

questions.overallExplanation: The Name box supplies the <fieldname> portion of EVAL-<fieldname> and the Eval Expression box supplies everything to the right of the equals sign. Both the alias form and the calculated field form scope to a host, a source, or a source type, and nothing else.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use calculated fields
guide.verdictNote: The conf settings are FIELDALIAS-<class> and EVAL-<fieldname>, both in props.conf. There is no ALIAS- or CALC- setting, despite both appearing in distractors.

docs.title: About calculated fields (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: The Splunk Web form separates the field name from the eval expression.

questions.stem: A source type already extracts a `status` field. A calculated field `EVAL-status` is then defined for the same source type. What happens?

options.text: The calculated field overrides the extracted field, even when its expression evaluates to null.
options.explanation: The override is unconditional. A null result replaces a perfectly good extracted value, which is the failure mode this rule exists to warn about.

options.text: The calculated field fills in only the events where status was not extracted.
options.explanation: That gap-filling behaviour has to be written explicitly with coalesce().

options.text: The extracted field wins, because extraction happens earlier in the sequence.
options.explanation: Running earlier does not confer precedence here. The later calculated field overwrites the value.

options.text: Both fields exist, as a multivalue field with two values.
options.explanation: No multivalue field is produced. One value replaces the other.

questions.overallExplanation: To preserve the extraction where it exists, write `EVAL-status = coalesce(status, <expression>)`. Without coalesce, an expression that returns null on some events silently deletes good data on those events.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use calculated fields
guide.verdictNote: This is the practical reason calculated fields are riskier than they look: they are not additive by default.

docs.title: About calculated fields (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: A calculated field overrides an extracted field of the same name, including when the expression is null.

questions.stem: Who can use a field alias immediately after it is created in Splunk Web?

options.text: Only the person who created it, until it is explicitly shared.
options.explanation: Knowledge objects are private on creation. Sharing to an app or globally is a separate step under Settings, Fields, then Permissions.

options.text: Everyone in the app where it was created.
options.explanation: App-level visibility requires sharing it to the app, which does not happen automatically.

options.text: Everyone on the deployment, since aliases are global objects.
options.explanation: Nothing about aliases makes them global by nature. They follow the same permission model as other knowledge objects.

options.text: Everyone with the same role as the creator.
options.explanation: Role membership is not the sharing mechanism. Permissions are set per object.

questions.overallExplanation: Private by default is the rule across knowledge objects: field extractions, aliases, calculated fields, event types, macros and workflow actions all start as Owner-scoped, and sharing is a deliberate second step.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use field aliases
guide.verdictNote: Objects shared only at app level are invisible to users working in a different app context until they are promoted to All apps.

docs.title: Manage knowledge object permissions (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Knowledge objects are private to their creator until shared.

questions.stem: The same field name appears in events from two different source types and needs the same alias in both. How many field alias configurations are required?

options.text: Two, because each alias is specific to a host, source, or source type.
options.explanation: Alias scope follows the props.conf stanza model, so a second source type needs its own definition.

options.text: One, because aliases are keyed on the field name.
options.explanation: Aliases are not global by field name. They are scoped like every other props.conf setting.

options.text: One, provided both source types are in the same index.
options.explanation: Index is not a scope for aliasing at all.

options.text: It depends on whether the two source types share a host.
options.explanation: Host is an alternative scope, not a modifier of source type scope.

questions.overallExplanation: Host, source, source type. That triple is the scope for field aliases, calculated fields and every other props.conf-driven setting. Index is never a scope, which rules out a whole family of distractors.

guide.blueprintTitle: Describe, create, and use field aliases
guide.verdictNote: The docs also warn against aliasing a field to the name of an internal field such as _time, because it produces unpredictable search results.

docs.title: Configure field aliases with props.conf (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Each field alias configuration is specific to events from a particular host, source, or source type.
